requirements.evidence: All contract routes present in routes/web.php:20-51 with the right names/methods/middleware (throttle:6,1 on password.email, signed on verification.verify, auth+verified on home). Login: strict email, auth.failed on email, lowercase email+IP limiter of 5 with auth.throttle, session()->regenerate(), redirectIntended(default: route('home')) (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:28-53). Register: str()->transliterate('register|'.$ip) with 5 attempts, error on email, Password::defaults(), Registered event, login + regenerate (Register.php:30-66). Reset rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset (PasswordResetController.php:65-71); single name="email" in reset view. MustVerifyEmail on User; EmailVerificationRequest gives 403 on tampered id; resend skips verified users. .env.example, phpunit.xml locale pins, lang/{en,pt_BR}/ui.php added. Not fully verifiable: requirement 9 also covers existing views (welcome, bulma-test) which the diff leaves untouched; the LocalizationTest scan only passes if they have no hardcoded href/action.

conventions.evidence: Livewire components validate with inline $this->validate([...]) arrays (Login.php:31-34, Register.php:36-40) rather than the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern. Repeated Bulma field markup (label/control/input/@error help) is copy-pasted across 4 views instead of an anonymous <x-...> component, and the two layouts duplicate the whole <head>. Otherwise good: named-route redirects, plain wire:model, {{ }} escaping, Fillable attribute kept, CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased], PHPDoc on public methods, Password::defaults() configured once in AppServiceProvider.

security.evidence: Per-email+IP and per-IP limiters inside the Livewire methods, session regeneration on login/register, session invalidate + regenerateToken on logout, forgot-password always returns passwords.sent, reset rotates remember_token, verification uses EmailVerificationRequest (403 on mismatched id/hash), all output escaped, no user-controlled IDs in Livewire state. Minor: layouts load Bulma from cdn.jsdelivr.net without SRI as a fallback (components/layouts/app.blade.php:14, guest.blade.php:14); the audit log records the raw attempted e-mail (Login.php:41).

tests.evidence: Six feature test files cover login (success, case-insensitive, intended redirect, auth.failed, unknown e-mail, validation, 5-try lockout, clear on success, remember token, audit log, guest-only), register (happy path, lowercase, password rule dataset, confirmed, unique/strict, IP limit, guest-only), password reset (sent/unknown same answer, 429 on 7th, single email input, remember_token rotation + event, bad token, rule, confirmation), verification (403 tamper test, edited signature, resend, verified no-mail, throttle, auth required), logout (CSRF rotation, POST-only, auth), localization (pt_BR/en pages, key parity, hardcoded-link scan).

simplicity.evidence: Lean, uses framework primitives (Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, RateLimiter, redirectGuestsTo/redirectUsersTo) with no extra layers. Some duplication: app and guest layouts share an identical <head> block (app.blade.php:1-18 vs guest.blade.php:1-18) and the form field markup repeats in every auth view.

readability.evidence: Small, focused classes with clear names (ensureIsNotRateLimited, throttleKey), short doc comments explaining intent (VerifyEmailController.php:12-16), consistent formatting, no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: auth controllers, Livewire components, views/layouts, lang files, locale config, phpunit pins, tests and the CHANGELOG entry. No SCSS/JS, Docker or mail-theme changes; config/app.php only changes the locale default.

issues.explanation: Livewire components validate with inline rule arrays instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute + $this->validate() pattern.

Requirement 9 extends the no-hardcoded-href/action rule to existing views, but the diff leaves them untouched, so it is unclear whether they comply. The new test scanning all views would fail if they do not.
The two layouts duplicate the entire <head>, and the Bulma field markup is copy-pasted across the auth views instead of going into an anonymous Blade component.
The fallback loads Bulma from a third-party CDN without a Subresource Integrity hash, which adds an unneeded supply-chain dependency.
Failed-login audit entries store the raw attempted e-mail (PII, possibly a mistyped password). Consider whether the logging policy allows this.

review.summary: The change builds the full session-auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, forgot/reset password, e-mail verification) with pt-BR-first translations, correct rate limiting, session hardening and remember-token rotation, plus thorough feature tests including tamper and throttle cases. Remaining issues are convention deviations (inline validation arrays instead of #[Validate], duplicated layout and field markup), a CDN fallback without SRI, and uncertainty about whether the untouched existing views comply with the no-hardcoded-links rule. I would approve with small changes.
